en.title: Pronouncing X Between Vowels
en.summary: Learn how to pronounce the Romanian letter x as a voiced gz sound between two vowels.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: The Romanian letter x often sounds like two blended consonants. Between two vowels, it makes a buzzing sound. It sounds like the letters 'g' and 'z' joined together. Listen to the word (examen) /e.ˈɡza.men/, which means exam. You hear this soft, vibrating sound right in the middle.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Start with the back of your tongue touching your soft palate. Release a quick 'g' sound with your vocal cords buzzing. Then, move the tip of your tongue near your front teeth. Push air out smoothly to make a 'z' sound. Keep your voice box vibrating for the whole sound.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Look at the letters around the letter x. When x sits between two vowels, say it as a buzzing sound. Listen to (exact) /eɡˈzakt/, which means exact. Also, listen to (exemplu) /eɡˈzem.plu/, which means example. In both words, vowels surround the letter x. Your voice stays on through both letters.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not whisper the sound like 'k' and 's'. Many learners turn off their voice too early. If you make a hiss, your voice box stops. Touch your throat while you speak. You should feel a strong vibration when you say (examen) /e.ˈɡza.men/.
